articles.title: College Football Playoff ranking, odds: Best bets to make, miss the CFP right now
articles.summary: Matt Russell gives his favorite futures wagers surrounding the College Football Playoff, ahead of Tuesday night's initial CFP rankings.
articles.body:
Last week, we looked at what NFL bets look the best around the midseason point of the season . This week, ahead of Tuesday night's initial College Football Playoff rankings reveal that will inspire bracket graphics throughout the land, bettors should be thinking about another crucial graphic.

Last year's first College Football Playoff rankings are below. It acts as a reminder that what's posted in early November is probably going to look a lot different by mid-December. Four of the 12 teams didn't end up making the playoff. Alabama went from having a bye to going on the road in the first round. And Miami didn't just make it in, it got to the National Championship game. While the first announcement feels important, betting opportunities should be ample with so many big games left to play.

As a framework for our betting, here's a projection of how many teams might make the playoff from each conference:

Starting here, you can work out the path to valuable bets on either side of the line of demarcation that is the CFP committee's top-12 teams.

If Texas beats Missouri this week, we'll be one game (LSU over Texas) away from the very real possibility that LSU, Texas, and Ole Miss, find themselves in a two-loss circle of results in the SEC.

Where might the CFP committee find a tiebreaker amidst that chaos?

Anyone who beats Georgia (and has enough other credentials) should get ranked ahead of the others.

Ole Miss has a free shot at an express pass to the CFP should the Rebels get a win at home over the Bulldogs this Saturday. Even if they don't top Georgia, who cares? Join the club. Wins over LSU, Missouri and the non-conference neutral site win over Louisville should get the Rebels rewarded. Having Trinidad Chambliss and a team that made a run last season definitely helps. Especially when the alternatives are Lane Kiffin, and the consistently tumultuous Texas.

Either BYU beats Utah, leaving the Utes potentially out of the Big 12 championship, or Utah beats BYU, and we likely get a "Holy War" rematch — which means two losses are going into that column in some way or another. Meanwhile, Texas Tech — having potentially found something offensively with the shift to Thomas Castellanos at quarterback — has a trip to Oklahoma State as its toughest task to finish the regular season at 11-1. They'd either get a shot in the Big 12 title game, or sit at home and watch either BYU or Utah take (at least) their second loss. For a committee that's valued record as the starting point for rankings, the Red Raiders are at least 50/50 to find their way in from the outside.

While you were sleeping, two major things happened in the Group of Six landscape late on Saturday:

Oregon State took a third loss (to Fresno State)

Boise State barely beat Texas State, but lost starting quarterback Maddux Madsen

Essentially, the entire Pac-12 took a hit. With Oregon State and Boise State set to play each other potentially twice, the Broncos will have to beat the Beavers twice with Max Cutforth at the helm, and if they don't, New Mexico should step right in as the "G6" Playoff nominee.

The Lobos' lone loss, 14-6 at Oklahoma, is impressive, and their tricky games down the stretch are at Wyoming (New Mexico should be a touchdown favorite), Air Force (on its third-string quarterback) and a likely home game for the conference title.

Before accounting for the vig, the Volunteers are deemed to have a better than 70% chance of beating Kentucky on Saturday, which would give the Vols the tiebreaker in the SEC over the Wildcats and Alabama Crimson Tide.

Tennessee's on its second quarterback, having gone away from Faizon Brandon (who took 10 sacks in a home loss to Texas) to George McIntyre, but the Vols defense might be the best in the conference (lowest EPA/Play allowed).

Their remaining road games come against two disappointing teams — Texas A&M and Vanderbilt — and the Vols get LSU at Neyland Stadium (the Tigers are 1-2 on the road). A good spot to earn another "tiebreaker" amidst the complex swirl of the SEC.

Long shot: South Carolina (12-1, DraftKings)

South Carolina, a school that many think deserved to get in after a hot finish to 2024, have a real opportunity to impress down the stretch, and, like most humans, committee members are prone to reacting to what they've seen most recently.

After dropping an overtime game to Kentucky, the Gamecocks blew out Florida at The Swamp, knocked off Tennessee and blew out Oklahoma in Norman. With three losses already, that's not enough to be more than barely ranked in the polls, but the Gamecocks are the other team with the opportunity to host Georgia.

They might be a touchdown underdog at home in that one, but with their other three games (vs. Texas A&M, at Arkansas, at Clemson) all winnable, at 12-1 odds, a potential seven-game winning streak (and not having to play in the SEC title game), with LaNorris Sellers at the helm, could have South Carolina in the tournament this time around.

Of course, even if it's just one of Tennessee or South Carolina in, profitable as current underdogs, some big-name teams might get left out.

In the same vein as above, LSU could also find itself in a scenario where it loses to Alabama, who lost to Tennessee, who could lose to LSU in Week 12 at Neyland Stadium, in a separate roundabout. However, two different favorites have to fall at home for this to happen, and we're trying to stay in line with the most likely results according to the betting market, as best we can.

So, can Alabama or LSU get in if it loses this Saturday?

With a loss, Alabama's best wins would then be at Kentucky, and on the road to South Carolina, without anything of note since September.

If LSU loses, the Tigers are in the same boat, as the Clemson blowout win to start the season looks more like no big deal, but at least they have two more chances to impress down the stretch (vs. Texas, at Tennessee). Plus, the Tigers are 5.5-point favorites at home this weekend (~66% to win).

Yet, the Tigers are +135 to miss the CFP, but the Tide are +225.

The SEC is going to end up with a loaded group of three-loss teams, and without winning in Baton Rouge, Alabama's "good wins" aren't going to stack up with the others.

Could they win as +185 underdogs in Baton Rouge? Of course, but holding a +225 ticket on Bama to miss the CFP has a great chance to gain value very soon.

The Big Ten is an Indiana win over USC in Week 11 away from having its own three-team carousel with Ohio State, making that trio untouchable from a betting perspective, but that doesn't mean they can't all get in. Of course, the Big Ten might just be a two-bid league, especially if this season's Cinderella has its Hollywood story turn into a pumpkin.

Whether it's Bob Chesney, or someone else over at UCLA, the Bruins are living a charmed life this season.

No. 5 in the AP poll, probably close to that in the first CFP rankings, and atop the Big Ten standings, give credit to UCLA for having won the games. However, its opponents are 17-23, three of the last four have been forced to play backup quarterbacks and another has already fired its head coach.

Maybe there's more good fortune in the future, but UCLA has to go to upset-minded Minnesota, host Illinois, go to Michigan, and then take on USC in the crosstown rivalry, which could decide a playoff spot in Week 13.

If the Bruins, with their own No. 2 quarterback Ty Dieffenbach (59% pass completions, 2 TD, INT, in two starts), drop two of those, they will either miss the Big Ten title game or set themselves up for a third loss in Indianapolis. All without a signature win, as Oregon's profile gets worse by the week.

Simply put, if Wake Forest loses at SMU in Week 11 or in the ACC title game, it's likely out of the mix for the College Football Playoff.

A loss to the Mustangs puts the Demon Deacons into a tiebreaker vortex for the conference, and they won't likely get a chance to get a signature win. Even if they do make the ACC title game, losing to Miami a second time will leave a bad taste on a team whose best win is over 5-3 Louisville.

The ACC is so lackluster that a two-loss non-champion is likely to get passed over in our "other" category by a team with three losses and better wins.

The mega-long shot: Miami (22-1, FanDuel)

November losses are nothing new to Miami, and the Hurricanes are already an underdog at Notre Dame this Saturday.

What if the Hurricanes don't win the ACC championship game?

The resume could indicate that they're just another two-loss team without a win over a ranked team, if Wake Forest drops a game down the stretch.

Miami would be anywhere from -6.5 to SMU to -10 in a rematch with Wake Forest, but the underdog moneyline wouldn't be anywhere near 22-1.

Based on value in the betting market alone , here's how the CFP top 12 could shake out:

The key to getting value out of a national championship futures bet is to back a team that ends up with the best possible path once the playoffs start.

We've discussed the probability of two- and three-loss teams making the College Football Playoff, which means if Notre Dame beats Miami on Saturday (effectively clinching a postseason berth), the Irish should earn a top-four seed, as others melt away record-wise.

Given the depth of contenders making up the eventual 5-11 seeds, it doesn't really matter which of the top four seeds Notre Dame gets, but its path to a first-round bye is the simplest: Just win in South Bend on Saturday night, and it won't matter whether the Irish are in the top four of the first CFP rankings on Tuesday night.

You can find more valuable betting analysis from Yahoo Sports betting contributor, Matt Russell , at THE WINDOW .

articles.title: Fantasy Football Panic Meter: Ravens are in trouble going into Week 9 after latest Lamar Jackson injury
articles.summary: Ray Garvin is worried about the Ravens, Vikings, but cautions not to give up on the Jaguars WR in his latest Panic Meter.
articles.body:
It's getting harder to give some of these offenses the benefit of the doubt. Coming out of Week 8, I'm sorting through where I'm willing to stay patient and where I'd rather make a move before things get worse.

We're in the early stages of Coping Corner with the Baltimore Ravens offense. Lamar Jackson injured his thumb on Baltimore's first offensive play in Week 8 and is now headed to injured reserve. That alone would have been a deflating afternoon for the Ravens and fantasy managers counting on this offense. Then Tyler Huntley went down, leaving undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to finish the game. Everybody loves the backup until the backup becomes the starter. We're now at the backup's backup.

You're still playing Derrick Henry, but I'm lowering my expectations. His 53 rushing yards and a touchdown gave you something usable, though that score came after a turnover put Baltimore at Buffalo's 17-yard line. Without Lamar, sustaining drives and creating those scoring opportunities becomes a much bigger concern. Henry can still give you a productive afternoon, but it doesn't feel like you have that same high-upside running back anymore.

The passing game? Man, it doesn't feel good. Zay Flowers ran 30 routes and earned five targets without catching a pass. Mark Andrews caught three passes for 14 yards, and to me, he looks well past his prime. I wasn't feeling good about him before Lamar went down. Losing Jackson only makes it harder to see where the production is going to come from. Any breakout thoughts you had about Ja'Kobi Lane took a hit, too. He ran 21 routes and saw one target.

Baltimore finished with 144 total yards. Fagnano completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards and an interception. This is the environment we're asking our fantasy players to produce in right now.

Yes, you're probably still playing Flowers. I'm not telling you to bench him regardless of your alternatives. But I would absolutely be open to trading him if someone is still valuing him like he's catching passes from a healthy Lamar. I want a usable starter back, but I'm willing to have that conversation before we get another look at how difficult this passing game could become. Losing Lamar takes the life out of this offense, and it's hard to see how things get much better anytime soon. With Andrews and Lane, I'm looking at my alternatives.

There was enough from Kyler Murray to keep Minnesota out of Total Panic. There wasn't enough to make me feel great about the entire offense.

Murray threw for 210 yards and two touchdowns while adding 35 yards on the ground. T.J. Hockenson caught four of his five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown, continuing to give us reasons to trust this connection. Through seven games, Hockenson has a 20.4% target share and is averaging 2.03 yards per route run. I'm comfortable treating him as a weekly top-12 tight end.

Justin Jefferson scored, but five catches for 33 yards isn't what you drafted him for. His frustration showed on the sideline, and he declined to speak with reporters afterward. He had nine targets and a 32.1% target share, so the ball was going his way. It still wasn't turning into the kind of production you expect from Jefferson. I understand the frustration, and I'm sure his fantasy managers do, too.

The secondary pieces are where my confidence starts to drop. Jordan Addison's season has been disappointing, although this game deserves some credit: eight targets, three catches and 66 yards while matching Jefferson's 33 routes. I'm not going to call that a disappearing act. I do need more consistency before I feel good counting on him.

The running game gave us much less to work with. Jordan Mason carried eight times for 20 yards. Aaron Jones Sr. managed 22 yards on five attempts. That's 42 rushing yards between them, with Murray individually outrushing either back.

Hockenson and Jefferson stay in your lineup. Beyond those two, I have questions about how much dependable fantasy production this offense can support.

We're a couple of weeks removed from Tetairoa McMillan's monster day, and now we're back to wondering when Carolina will put the whole thing together.

McMillan finished with six catches for 58 yards against Green Bay. The frustrating part is that the workload was there. He had 11 targets, a 31.4% target share and more than half of Carolina's targeted air yards. That is plenty of opportunity to deliver a much bigger afternoon.

Bryce Young completed 23-of-41 passes for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception. He was sacked six times. Carolina was also without offensive linemen Damien Lewis and Torricelli Simpkins III, which certainly didn't help an offense already struggling to turn opportunities into production.

I've got Some Panic with McMillan, but those 11 targets keep me from recommending a massive change. His season target share sits at 26.4%. He's still getting the kind of involvement I want to bet on, even if living with the results has been frustrating.

Jalen Coker belongs in Some Panic, too. His touchdown helped, but it accounted for 26 of his 36 receiving yards. He caught two passes on five targets. I'm glad we got the score. I'm not suddenly comfortable with the weekly floor.

Chuba Hubbard gets No Panic from me. He handled 22 carries for 81 yards and a touchdown, then added seven receptions for 38 yards. That's 29 touches and 119 scrimmage yards in a game where the passing offense struggled. He kept finding ways to produce.

I'm still playing McMillan and Hubbard. With Coker, I'm accepting a much wider range of outcomes. You're going to have to live with some volatility here rather than overhaul your lineup.

I'm not panicking on P-Wash. I am going to keep reminding people that Jacksonville doesn't feel like an offense with the same clear-cut No. 1 option every week. I talked about this with Matt Harmon on the Data Dump Tuesday show. When everything is clicking for Washington, the usage can be outstanding. But Lawrence will get the ball to the open man, and that isn't going to be Washington every week.

Against Indianapolis, he caught one pass for 16 yards on two targets and added 10 rushing yards. Jacksonville won 42-7 after leading 28-0 at halftime. Trevor Lawrence attempted just 14 passes before his day was over early in the fourth quarter. Bhayshul Tuten ran for 104 yards and scored both on the ground and through the air. This offense had plenty working without needing a big Washington game.

In his last game before the bye, Washington caught four passes for 64 yards against Houston but still drew 11 targets. The fantasy results weren't what you wanted in either game, but the opportunities were very different.

Across seven games, Washington has a 24.5% target share and has drawn a target on 25.3% of his routes. We also saw him turn six catches into 124 yards and two touchdowns against Philadelphia. That's the ceiling I'm still betting on.

To me, Washington still has the highest receiving ceiling in this offense. I'm embracing the variance that comes with it. One bad afternoon in a blowout versus a terrible Colts team isn't enough to move me off him.

articles.title: Tenerife striker’s death after on-field collision a painful reminder for Indian football fans
articles.summary: Panaji: CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died after colliding with a rival player during a Spanish second- division match Monday.
articles.body: Panaji: CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died after colliding with a rival player during a Spanish second- division match Monday.The 30-year-old, who was chasing a pass on the break into the rival half, collided heavily with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his penalty area, and suffered head and chest injuries. The striker received treatment on the pitch for about 15 minutes before being taken to hospital.The goalkeeper was sent off, and the match was abandoned due to the seriousness of the injury.Tenerife initially said De Miguel’s “situation is stable but remains serious.” His condition worsened and he was pronounced dead early Tuesday morning.“Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, we at CD Tenerife announce the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,” the club said in a statement on Tuesday. “There are no words of comfort. There is absolutely nothing that can ease this overwhelming sense of sadness.”When the incident occurred, Tenerife and Andorra were tied 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time. De Miguel chased a long ball that was lobbed into the opposite half but clashed with Owono, who had raced towards the halfway mark. The goalkeeper’s knee appeared to collide with the striker after which he fell, and lay motionless on the pitch.The incident will be a painful reminder for Indian football fans of a similar on-field clash, and death, when Dempo SC striker Cristiano Junior collided with Mohun Bagan goalkeeper Subrata Paul in the final of the Federation Cup in 2004. The match continued for the remaining 12 minutes while the Brazilian was taken to the hospital, where he was declared brought dead.Hailing from Madrid, De Miguel started his career at Leganes and went on to play for eight different lower-division clubs in Spain. He signed for Tenerife at the start of the 2025-26 season and scored 11 league goals in his first year, helping Tenerife win a long-awaited promotion to the Segunda Division.At the start of the season, he attracted interest from Mohun Bagan SG. The former Indian Super League champions and among the biggest spenders in India were on the hunt for a top-notch striker following the departure of former Australian World Cupper Jason Cummings.“We had a call with Jesus and his representative,” a senior Bagan official told TOI. “He said he was keen to come to India but there were two years remaining on his existing contract with Tenerife, so we could not make the transfer work. Jesus has scored consistently in the lower divisions in Spain and would have clicked in ISL.”Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. They said on Tuesday that proceedings were opened and prosecutors will also be involved.Andorra, which is owned by former Barcelona star Gerard Pique, also offered its condolences, along with other clubs, the Spanish soccer federation and La Liga. “We wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife. May he rest in peace,” Andorra said in a statement.The Real Madrid players held a minute’s silence for De Miguel during training, while Espanyol postponed the presentation of their new coach.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Manchester United 3-2 Roma: Bruno Fernandes claims players don't need to save Michael Carrick's job after first win in 10 games
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes feels Manchester United players didn't need to save Michael Carrick's job in their 3-2 comeback win over Roma; Carrick's side avoided going ten games without a win for the first time in over four decades
articles.body:
United and Carrick looked dead and buried within the first 18 minutes as the Italian side took a two-goal lead in the early exchanges.

It prompted boos and protests from supporters, who threw tennis balls onto the pitch, but the Red Devils turned things around as a Fernandes penalty and a late Matheus Cunha double gave them their first win in 54 days.

The spirit shown in the performance suggested at least some on-pitch support for Carrick, whose tenure appeared to have been hanging on by a thread ever since the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth .

Fernandes was named on the bench for that game after publicly questioning the tactics in a sobering 4-1 defeat to Como four days prior. His words after Roma, though, were a lot more defiant than accusatory.

"We don't need to save anyone's job," Fernandes told Amazon Prime post-match.

"We've been working so hard to get out of this situation altogether. It's been tough. There's been a lot of speculation in the media, a lot of lies around many things that have happened in this club. Between me and the manager, that we had to clear the air. Nothing like that happened.

"The manager took a decision of putting myself on the bench because I wasn't performing at that level. Everyone felt that it was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right.

"The manager is the one who makes the decisions. I have to accept them, I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, in the staff and every player that is in this club. It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me. It should be [a turning point]."

Carrick himself similarly played down suggestions that the turnaround could've helped his cause, saying "it's a win for us as a football club", when asked how the result could change the narrative.

"We've shown a lot of character as a group to weather what we've had to. You find out a lot about each other, the players will find out things about me. I certainly do about them and their character and what it means to them and what they're prepared to put in."

The win, and the nature of it, feels very reminiscent of a 2018 3-2 win over Newcastle during Jose Mourinho's time at the club. Two early goals stunned the home side, who were already under immense pressure for their poor start to the season.

In the second half, a response. A player who reportedly had his issues with Mourinho, Anthony Martial, found the net en route to a comeback which was secured by a severely underperforming South American in Alexis Sanchez.

On Tuesday night, the role of Mourinho was played by Carrick. The role of Martial you could argue was played by Fernandes, regardless of how he feels his comments following Como were perceived. And the role of Sanchez was bettered by Cunha's heroics.

Did it save Mourinho his job? Ultimately, it didn't. He was sacked by December that year, but maybe it gave him a bit more time at the helm.

In the 10 games prior to the Newcastle win, Mourinho's United had only won three times. In the 13 after, they picked up five, plus draws against Chelsea and Arsenal that weren't to be scoffed at. The issue was, the expectations at United were higher in 2018, and that return wasn't cutting it.

In reality, if Carrick managed a run of five wins, four draws and four defeats over the next 13 games, he probably isn't shown the door and is given more time to build on the project. Especially if there are some disagreements from the higher-ups on who should be the man to replace him if they went down that route.

There is just one variable that will make or break things for Carrick. Can he go back-to-back? If his United side can beat Aston Villa on Sunday, it could be the statement the former midfielder needs to earn him more time.

Unai Emery is widely regarded as the best boss in the Premier League. If Carrick is sacked, many United fans would be begging to see him take the hot seat. But, with the spirit and belief in the dressing room higher than it has been in two months following Tuesday's spectacular comeback, Carrick has a chance to get one over on Emery and leave a final impression on his bosses before the international break.

It won't be until Sunday evening, when the final whistle is blown at Old Trafford, that we will truly know whether or not Carrick's men saved his job, rather appropriately, in Fergie time.

articles.title: El pecado de Le Normand
articles.standfirst: 'En Copa de Balón', una opinión de Elías Israel
articles.summary: 'En Copa de Balón', una opinión de Elías Israel
articles.body: El Atlético es peor equipo que el Bayern. Sin embargo, la obra de Simeone es tan bestial en los tres últimos lustros que todos nos hemos creído que el Atleti está obligado a mirarle a los ojos a cualquier gigante de Europa, mucho más si se juega en el Metropolitano. La diferencia presupuestaria y de calidad no es ningún descrédito, cuando hablamos del gigante alemán, que tiene en su ataque al reciente Balón de Oro, Harry Kane, o al futbolista más llamativo del planeta fútbol, Michael Olise. Aún así, el campeón alemán no necesitó el brillo de sus estrellas para tumbar al equipo de Simeone. El Bayern es uno de los pocos equipos que puede cuestionar el favoritismo del PSG en esta Champions. Para competir en igualdad un duelo asimétrico hay que hacer muchas cosas bien y no cometer ningún error grosero. Le Normand cometió un fallo tan grande como la envergadura del partido. Se embolicó con el balón, en lugar de sacarlo de su área, y Lennart Karl estuvo espabilado para silenciar el Metropolitano. Nunca sabremos si la decisión de Simeone de sustituirlo fue un señalamiento o la búsqueda de otras alternativas, pero Le Normand se fue tan cabreado consigo mismo que se quitó de encima el saludo y, de paso, a su propio entrenador. La que no se va a poder sacar tan fácil de encima es la sombra del Cuti Romero, el central titular, que le volverá a dar otra jerarquía a la defensa rojiblanca, cuando recupere el tono físico. Esa jugada cambió el signo del partido y, a partir de ese momento, la gestualidad de Simeone, que casi es el retrato más inconfundible del estado de ánimo rojiblanco. El Atleti nunca se levantó de ese error. Recibió, esta vez sí, un golazo de Laimer, que fue una pesadilla durante todo el partido. Pudieron ser más. A partir del error se constató que un bulldozer pasaba por el Metropolitano. Perder en una noche en la que se mide la grandeza siempre duele. Que el Bayern sea mejor se asume; lo que escuece es no haber tenido siquiera la oportunidad de comprobarlo, porque un error de bulto cambió el partido. Y justo en vísperas de recibir al Barcelona, con el liderato en juego. P.D.: La vida debería ser más importante que el fútbol y la pérdida de Jesús de Miguel debería haber paralizado la jornada de Champions, al menos en territorio español, en el día de hoy.

articles.title: Raphinha juega a ritmo de dobletes
articles.standfirst: Suma cinco y encadena dos: ha recuperado su excelente nivel de antes de la lesión
articles.summary: Suma cinco y encadena dos: ha recuperado su excelente nivel de antes de la lesión
articles.body: Si contra el Alavés, el Barça confirmó que la derrota en el Clásico en LaLiga fue un accidente. Ayer, contra el Aston Villa, reiteró que su tropiezo en París en la Champions League fue también un hecho puntual. El Barcelona ganó al equipo de Emery, invicto hasta esta jornada, y lo hizo con otra goleada más. El protagonista de la noche fue, de nuevo, Raphinha. El extremo brasileño ha recuperado el histórico y excelente nivel que tenía antes de la lesión que sufrió en octubre. El exjugador del Leeds firmó anoche un doblete. Uno más. Ya marcó dos tantos contra el Feyenoord, en la Champions League, y frente a Elche, Rayo y Alavés, en LaLiga. Precisamente, el conjunto vasco fue el último contrincante del Barça, el pasado fin de semana. Raphinha también vio puerta en el Clásico, por lo que ya encadena tres encuentros viendo puerta. Está en racha. Sigue en racha. Tras regresar de la concentración con Brasil en octubre con un edema muscular en la parte posterior del muslo derecho y ser baja contra el Galatasaray en Europa y el Getafe en el torneo doméstico, ha recuperado su gran nivel de antes de la dolencia. Imparable Raphinha, que también ha celebrado dos hat-tricks (contra Racing y Sevilla en LaLiga), está protagonizando una campaña histórica. Ya suma ¡19! goles esta temporada, en los 13 encuentros en los que ha participado. Su reconversión en delantero centro ha sido todo un éxito. Y eso que el capitán azulgrana no duda en sacrificarse en labores defensivas y en ser un ejemplo en la presión cuando el rival tiene el balón. Anoche volvió a firmar un encuentro modélico en todas las facetas.

articles.title: Raphinha se olvida del fútbol y recuerda a Jesús de Miguel: «Hoy es un día muy duro»
articles.summary: El brasileño, autor de dos goles ante el Aston Villa, dedicó sus primeras palabras a la familia del futbolista del CD Tenerife y reconoció la dificultad de a...
articles.body:
El brasileño, autor de dos goles ante el Aston Villa, dedicó sus primeras palabras a la familia del futbolista del CD Tenerife y reconoció la dificultad de afrontar el encuentro tras conocer la noticia.

Raphinha fue uno de los grandes protagonistas de la victoria del FC Barcelona ante el Aston Villa, pero su actuación quedó en un segundo plano al finalizar el encuentro. El delantero brasileño, autor de un doblete, quiso dejar a un lado el resultado y los goles para acordarse de Jesús de Miguel , futbolista del CD Tenerife fallecido este martes a los 30 años.

En declaraciones a Movistar +, el azulgrana trasladó sus condolencias a los familiares y allegados del jugador.

«No quiero hablar de fútbol. Quiero dedicar la victoria a la afición. Quiero mandar mucha fuerza a la familia de Jesús y que descanse en paz. Hoy no es un día para hablar de fútbol», expresó el brasileño.

La noticia del fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel también tuvo un fuerte impacto en el entorno del Barcelona. Raphinha reconoció que los jugadores conocieron lo sucedido antes del encuentro y que resultó especialmente complicado concentrarse en la competición.

«Esto le puede pasar a cualquiera. Es muy duro, cuando hemos visto la noticia… es complicado. Piensas que tienes que jugar también», explicó el atacante, poniendo voz a los sentimientos que acompañaron al equipo durante una jornada marcada por la tristeza.

Sobre el terreno de juego, Raphinha había firmado una actuación destacada con dos tantos que contribuyeron al triunfo azulgrana frente al Aston Villa. Sin embargo, el brasileño insistió en que no era el momento de detenerse en su rendimiento individual ni en el resultado.

«Hoy no es un buen día para hablar de fútbol y quiero mandar mucho ánimo para la familia de Jesús», concluyó ante los micrófonos de Movistar +.

De esta manera, el delantero del Barça quiso dedicar la victoria y su actuación a Jesús de Miguel, sumándose a las numerosas muestras de cariño que el fútbol español está trasladando a su familia, al CD Tenerife y a toda la afición blanquiazul.

articles.title: Rodri injury mars easy win for Barcelona over Emery's Villa in front of Prince William
articles.summary: Barcelona's joy at an impressive win in the Champions League was tempered by an injury to star midfielder Rodri.Spain's World Cup-winning captain was forced...
articles.body:
Barcelona's joy at an impressive win in the Champions League was tempered by an injury to star midfielder Rodri.

Spain's World Cup-winning captain was forced off with a suspected calf injury at halftime of Tuesday's 3-0 victory over Aston Villa, which was earned by an early goal from Lamine Yamal and Raphinha's second-half double.

The injury to Rodri will be a concern for his team, which visits Atletico Madrid on Sunday in a top-of-the-table match in La Liga. Barcelona leads by two points from Atleti.

Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said Rodri "felt some muscular pain."

"It'll need to wait until Wednesday before we examine that and find out more," Flick added.

It was otherwise a positive night for Barcelona at Camp Nou in front of Prince William , the heir to the British throne and Villa's most famous fan.

Yamal got his 14th Champions League goal — more than anyone else under the age of 20 — when he intercepted a stray pass from Joao Gomes following a goal kick, cut inside and bent a finish into the bottom corner in the seventh minute.

Rodri coming off, to be replaced by Marc Bernal, didn't hold back Barca, with Raphinha scuffing a shot into the corner in the 52nd and then meeting an impudent, outside-of-the-foot cross by Joao Cancelo with a first-time finish in the 64th.

It marked a miserable return to the Camp Nou for Villa coach Unai Emery , who was last at the stadium when in charge of a Paris Saint-Germain team that arrived with a 4-0 lead from the first leg in the round of 16 in 2017. Barcelona won the second leg 6-1 in a recovery now widely known as "La Remontada" (The Comeback).

Villa dropped points for the first time this campaign, after opening with three straight wins.

"We need to learn, draw conclusions, and figure out how to compete better," Emery said. "We have to be capable of staying competitive against the favorites, like Barca."

articles.title: Champions League comebacks: What are the other best after Manchester United beat Roma
articles.summary: Manchester United come from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 - but what are the other best fightbacks in Champions League history?
articles.body:
Manchester United came from two goals down to beat Roma in a dramatic Champions League tie on Tuesday to give manager Michael Carrick a much-needed boost as he fights to save his job.

Things were looking bleak at Old Trafford when his side found themselves 2-0 down after just 17 minutes against their Italian visitors, who had not lost in their 10 Serie A games this season.

A nine-game winless run had left Carrick's position increasingly precarious and a poor start left United facing another damaging defeat.

But they stormed back in the second half with a show of character and class that had been missing in a troubled campaign where they had previously won just twice in all competitions.

Captain Bruno Fernandes started the fightback from the penalty spot before Matheus Cunha struck twice in the space of three memorable minutes to turn the game on its head.

What had threatened to be another night to forget became unforgettable for the Old Trafford faithful, while Carrick could breathe a little easier after his side pulled off an unlikely success.

United, though, are hardly the first side to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat on Europe's biggest stage.

Here are some of the greatest comebacks in Champions League history.

Man Utd produce incredible second-half comeback to beat Roma

'We don't need to save anyone's job,' says Man Utd captain Fernandes

Ajax 2-3 Tottenham (semi-final second leg, 8 May 2019, 3-3 on agg, Spurs win on away goals)

Tottenham travelled to Ajax for the second leg of their semi-final trailing 1-0, and things went from bad to worse in Amsterdam when Matthijs de Ligt and Hakim Ziyech put Ajax 3-0 ahead on aggregate before the break.

Spurs needed to score three times without reply to progress on away goals, and were given a glimmer of hope 10 minutes into the second half through Lucas Moura - and it was game on just four minutes later.

Moura pounced on a loose ball in the box after Fernando Llorente's shot was saved and he curled home to put the hosts on the ropes.

The stunning turnaround was completed in the 95th minute when Moura recorded a hat-trick to seal Tottenham's spot in the final on away goals, leaving Ajax players strewn across the turf in disbelief.

Liverpool 4-0 Barcelona (semi-final second leg, 7 May 2019, 4-3 on agg)

Just 24 hours before Tottenham's heroics in Amsterdam, Liverpool had overturned their own three-goal deficit.

The Reds' hopes of forcing their way back into the semi-final after a 3-0 loss to Barcelona at the Nou Camp looked slim, especially with Mohamed Salah and Roberto Firmino unavailable because of injury.

But Divock Origi got the ball rolling on seven minutes, before the tie really turned in the space of 166 seconds after half-time when substitute Georginio Wijnaldum scored twice.

A moment of quick thinking saw Liverpool complete the job as Trent Alexander-Arnold spotted Barcelona's defence switch off from a corner, whipping the ball in low for Origi to fire home and spark wild scenes at Anfield.

Roma 3-0 Barcelona (quarter-final second leg, 10 April 2018, 4-4 on agg, Roma win on away goals)

That iconic line from commentator Peter Drury summed up an incredible night as Roma clinched a memorable comeback to send Barcelona packing in the quarter-finals.

Own goals from Daniele de Rossi and Kostas Manolas helped Barca record a 4-1 win in the first leg at the Nou Camp.

Edin Dzeko's late goal in Spain gave Roma something to build from and the forward struck early in the return leg to further strengthen their belief.

De Rossi atoned for his own goal with a second-half strike and, with just eight minutes to go, Manolas headed home a corner to end Roma's 34-year wait for a place in the semi-finals of Europe's leading competition.

Barcelona 6-1 Paris St-Germain (last-16 second leg, 8 March 2017, 6-5 on agg)

Arguably the greatest comeback of all, this one is so iconic that it has its very own title in France and Spain - La Remontada (The Comeback).

PSG were clinical at home, winning 4-0, but the Nou Camp sensed something special when Luis Suarez scored after just three minutes in the second leg.

Barcelona were two goals to the good at the break courtesy of a Layvin Kurzawa own goal, but still trailed by two goals on aggregate.

Lionel Messi scored a penalty soon after the restart but Edinson Cavani hit back to silence the home faithful, although it wasn't the pendulum-swinging moment PSG hoped for.

Barcelona, now trailing 5-3, needed three goals in fewer than 30 minutes to achieve a miracle. Neymar scored a free-kick in the 88th minute to offer further hope, before the Brazilian stroked home a 91st-minute penalty to level the tie at 5-5 on aggregate.

But PSG were still heading through on away goals.

Then, with 20 seconds of added time remaining, La Remontada came to fruition when Sergi Roberto turned home Neymar's chipped pass, with Barcelona becoming the only team in history to overturn a four-goal Champions League deficit.

Deportivo La Coruna 4-0 AC Milan (quarter-final second leg, 7 April 2004, 5-4 on agg)

Deportivo La Coruna, currently plying their trade in the second tier of Spanish football, are no longer associated with the Champions League - but they carried out an unforgettable fightback against heavyweight opposition in 2004.

Milan travelled to Spain with a 4-1 lead from the first leg, but Deportivo were not ready to roll over.

Walter Pandiani, who broke the deadlock at the San Siro, got the Spaniards up and running on home soil.

Unlike the first leg when they sat back after taking the lead, Deportivo threw caution to the wind and it paid off as they wiped out Milan's aggregate advantage in just 43 minutes after goals from Juan Carlos Valeron and Albert Luque.

That would have been enough for Deportivo to go through on away goals but they continued to press and Fran slotted home a fourth to confirm Carlo Ancelotti's side were heading out.

articles.title: Jesus de Miguel: Tributes paid across Europe to Tenerife striker
articles.summary: Tributes were paid across Tuesday's Champions League fixtures to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died following collision on the pitch.
articles.body:
The world of football has come together to mourn the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel .

The forward suffered head and chest injuries in a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Spanish second division match against FC Andorra on Monday.

De Miguel's condition was described as stable but serious on Monday, but his health deteriorated on Tuesday morning and the Spaniard died at 07:00 GMT.

A minute's silence was held before Tuesday evening's Champions League matches across Europe.

That will be repeated for Wednesday's fixtures, as well as all Europa League and Conference League matches this week.

Mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez, Tenerife's home ground.

Tenerife said in a statement on Tuesday evening they will commence six official days of mourning, with all club activities suspended during this time.

The club's players, staff and officials will attend De Miguel's funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, Toledo.

Tenerife will also open their home ground on Saturday evening to allow supporters to "bid a fitting farewell".

"Jesus de Miguel's family would like to thank everyone for their messages of support and, from the bottom of their hearts, ask that their privacy be respected at this terrible time. May he rest in peace," added the statement.

"We are torn by the news," said Fran Leon, president of Tenerife's federation of supporters' clubs.

"All of the island is in mourning. All of Canarias is in mourning. It's a shared pain."

Fan David Tejera said De Miguel's "effort" and "passion" for Tenerife would endure.

"You are already part of the blue and white history," he said.

Tenerife and Andorra were tied 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred.

Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.

The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's ground to hospital.

Players from both teams were visibly distressed by the incident, with a number of De Miguel's team-mates in tears.

Reuters reported on Tuesday that police in Spain have opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel's death.

Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui told Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings were "very unlikely".

The referee showed Owono a straight red card before abandoning the match.

The goalkeeper, who had over 30,000 followers on Instagram on Tuesday morning, has since deactivated his account.

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho expressed his sadness over the incident and said it is a "very, very difficult moment" for Owono.

"I think it's something very shocking for the world in general, so imagine for the world of football, for people like us who are on the pitch competing every day," he said.

"It's hard, it's sad. Obviously, all our words and feelings go out to the family and friends of the player who passed away, and I also think this has to be a very, very, very difficult moment for the other player [Owono] involved in the situation.

After scoring twice in Barcelona's win over Aston Villa, Brazilian forward Raphinha said: "Today I don't want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus - may he rest in peace.

"From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family."

De Miguel had been at Tenerife for just over a season, having joined in the summer of 2025 from Castellon. The striker helped the team gain promotion to the second division.

The Spanish forward began his career with Leganes at youth level in the Madrid suburbs, playing for a string of teams, including Unionistas de Salamanca, before signing for Castellon in 2023.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said at a news conference the incident was "heartbreaking".

"To see a colleague lose his life in such a manner, it's beyond any words that I can put today," said the Spanish coach.

Other sports stars, including retired Spanish tennis icon Rafael Nadal, Argentine great Lionel Messi, and Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo also left messages on Instagram.

"There are no words. My condolences and lots of strength to all his family and friends," wrote Inter Miami forward Messi.

Nadal expressed a "terrible sadness" at De Miguel's passing "from the bottom of my heart".

"Lots of strength to the family. May he rest in peace."

Former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, who co-owns Andorra, said: "I am sorry with all my soul. Rest in peace, Jesus."

De Miguel's Tenerife team-mates also paid tribute on social media.

Midfielder Juanjo Sanchez said: "You let me into your heart, and you earned a place in mine, as we shared moments of laughter every single day and took walks barefoot after our training sessions.

"I cannot let this moment pass without highlighting what a wonderful person you are. You never had an unkind word or a sour expression for anyone, and you always displayed exemplary conduct, despite all the challenges you faced.

"You will always be with me, my friend."

Striker Enric Gallego described De Miguel as "one of the best people" he has met, in an emotional statement.

"Thank you for everything we experienced together - for your camaraderie, your character, your humanity and the exemplary attitude you always showed," he said.

"I feel very fortunate to have shared a locker room with you. I'm going to miss you so much."

Forward Fran Sabina said: "There is no explanation or words that make sense of something like this.

"You were an important person in my life.

"We were lucky enough to share unforgettable moments, laughter, stories and experiences that today become memories that I will cherish forever in my heart.

"Thank you my friend. Thank you for every moment lived, for every shared experience, for the laughter, for your affection and, most of all, for this sincere friendship that we had.

"The appreciation we had was mutual. And that's something neither time nor your absence can ever change."

However, the report did not provide any details suggesting that they were romantically involved.The rumors had gained attention partly because both are connected to the same university. Kai is part of the women's golf program, while Weinberg plays for the Miami Hurricanes football team.Kai is the daughter of Donald Trump Jr. and Vanessa Trump. She joined the University of Miami for the 2026-27 academic year and is now in her freshman year.Her main focus at college is golf. She has competed in several junior tournaments and has been working toward her long-term goal of becoming a professional golfer.Jake Weinberg's Strong Season With Miami Hurricanes Adds To His ProfileWhile his personal life has become a topic of online discussion, Jake Weinberg has also been having a good season on the football field.The Boynton Beach, Florida, native previously played for Florida State before transferring to Miami. articles.title: Aston Villa: Boss Unai Emery takes positives from Barcelona defeat
articles.summary: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery says his team have "work to do" to reach Barcelona's level after a 3-0 Champions League defeat at the Nou Camp.
articles.body:
Unai Emery punched the air in frustration at the Spotify Nou Camp.

It came from a place of disappointment and exasperation as his Aston Villa side let slip the opportunity of a result in their Champions League tie against Barcelona.

They had just fallen 2-0 behind in Spain, having tried to match the hosts blow-for-blow.

Raphinha's quick second-half double put the game out of reach after Lamine Yamal's opener, when Villa pressed the self-destruct button just seven minutes in.

It could have led to a collapse but, instead, they took the game to the Spanish champions during an engrossing first half, which could - and perhaps should - have yielded a leveller.

While defeat ended their 100% Champions League start after three wins, it gave Villa and boss Emery the chance to consider their progress.

Barcelona brilliance ends Villa's perfect start

Villa firmly believe they belong on this stage. After four years of improvement with Emery they have another chance to prove it.

They arrived in Spain with wins against Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, but this was their hardest test.

Emery, who celebrated his 55th birthday on Tuesday, wanted to use it as a barometer for their progress, to see how they compared with the current La Liga leaders and five-time European champions.

In the driving rain Villa could argue they matched Barca in the opening period and had it not been for Joao Gomes' glaring error that led to Lamine Yamal's strike, and poor finishing, they could have snatched the advantage.

Yet they fell short. They have been on the rise under Emery but last season's Europa League winners showed they are still not at the level to win in the Nou Camp.

The head coach would also deny it, but perhaps he had something to prove in this stadium which handed him his harshest lesson in the competition nine years ago.

In what became known as La Remontada [The Comeback], Barcelona recovered from 4-0 down from the first leg of their last-16 tie to beat Emery's Paris St-Germain side 6-1 in the home return and 6-5 on aggregate.

"One more match. Just one more match," said Emery when asked about it on Monday.

There was to be no Villa comeback on Tuesday night and Emery's record at the Nou Camp now stands at 15 defeats in 16 games and, in 31 attempts against Barca, he had won just three times.

He was able to field what was his strongest available team, but they created their own problems when Gomes' wretched pass gifted Lamine Yamal the crucial opener.

Emery, whose side were overtaken by second-placed Barcelona in the league phase table, added: "We are working for years together and we made mistakes like that but we have always overcome those mistakes. I am not blaming him."

The self-inflicted wound, though, failed to discourage Villa as they refused to lie down and accept a Barcelona victory.

Barca were without Andreas Christensen, Eric García and Xavi Espart, leaving them fragile in defence, with 20-year-old midfielder Brian Farinas making his Champions League debut and just second start at right-back.

The hosts had not kept a Champions League clean sheet in 18 games, a run stretching back to April 2025, and there was real fear from seasoned Barca watchers that Villa would exploit their weakness.

In the first half Matty Cash, Gomes and Johan Manzambi, twice, made Barca sweat as the visitors created chances without taking them.

German Leon Goretzka hit the post in the second half but by then the game was done after Raphinha's strikes.

Lamine Yamal, Anthony Gordon and Joao Cancelo went close to adding to Barca's tally, but Emery remained philosophical.

"The test was definitely not in the level we want to achieve but there are a lot of things to learn, a lot of experience for the players and us," he said. "It is giving me a lot of information to analyse and compete at this level.

"Overall, we are competing fantastically in the Champions League, although playing the match we played we have work to do to get to this level [of Barcelona].

"We were sometimes achieving it and close to scoring goals but we must be ruthless in the attacking third, 3-0 is maybe more than we deserved, but we accept the defeat."

It was still a reminder of how far Villa have come under Emery, who took over when they were three points above the Premier League relegation zone.

A Champions League night against Barcelona in the Nou Camp was fanciful when the Spaniard walked in the door from Villarreal.

Since then, he has delivered the Europa League title and two Champions League campaigns and this defeat in Spain will be another key marker in Villa's journey with him as they now prepare to visit Manchester United next on Sunday.

"Barcelona made the right decisions at the right times and scored really good goals," captain John McGinn told TNT Sports.

"The manager spoke about being clinical at important moments in the game. When you come here, 50-50s sometimes don't go your way. They also leave players up the pitch so if you lose the ball they can be away.

"I think we are competitive against teams at this level, we have shown that whether it is Bayern Munich or PSG. It was a huge learning curve for us and I am sure it will stand us in good stead for the future."

articles.title: Brian Kelly Interested in FSU Job After Notre Dame, LSU Stints, 'Would be an Honor'
articles.summary: Brian Kelly certainly seems open to the head-coaching vacancy at Florida State after the program fired Mike Norvell.
articles.body:
Brian Kelly certainly seems open to the head-coaching vacancy at Florida State after the program fired Mike Norvell.

"Yeah, I mean, look, when you're talking to an unemployed football coach, every job's a great job, you know? But Florida State, look, I've got a great history with Florida State, great games," he said on College Sports Radio on Sirius XM (h/t Nick Kosko of On3). "I know what that's like, the history and tradition of Florida State, playing in that state, and the fan base. So anytime you have an incredibly brand driven, great tradition and history, there's a want and desire to be part of somebody that has had that success and, certainly, leading that program, from anyone's perspective, would be an honor and privilege."

Kelly, 65, last coached LSU in the 2025 campaign before being fired midseason and ultimately replaced by Lane Kiffin. In stints leading Central Michigan (2004-06), Cincinnati (2006-09), Notre Dame (2010-21) and LSU (2022-25) he's posted a career 200-76 record (officially 179-76 after the NCAA vacated the school's wins in 2012-13 due to an academic infraction ).

Florida State seems likely to cast a wide net in its coaching search as it seeks to return to national prominence. Consider Kelly among those willing to throw his hat into the ring.

articles.title: College Football Playoff 2026 Rankings Released Ahead of Week 10
articles.summary: The first College Football Playoff rankings of the 2026 season were revealed on Tuesday as the homestretch of the campaign begins over the weekend.
articles.body:
The first College Football Playoff rankings of the 2026 season were revealed on Tuesday as the homestretch of the campaign begins over the weekend.

Miami's spot at the top of the rankings shouldn't come as much of a surprise. The Hurricanes, who are also No. 1 in the AP Poll, are undefeated heading into their matchup against Notre Dame, a game that should shake up next week's rankings.

Miami has had a few close calls, like a one-score win over Florida State and a three-point win over North Carolina last week, but last year's national championship game runner-up has otherwise been dominant.

Clearly, Georgia's upset loss to Auburn didn't scare off the selection committee too much, and that's likely because of the Bulldogs' strong wins over Alabama and Florida.

Kirby Smart's squad has a gauntlet on deck, as it will face ranked opponents in its next three games.

While Utah has just one ranked win, the Utes are undefeated through eight games and have impressed the committee enough to establish themselves among the top teams. They'll face BYU on Saturday in a game that will carry plenty of CFP implications.

Alabama at No. 5 is certainly a bit of a head-scratcher, considering the Crimson Tide suffered a blowout loss to Tennessee, which is ranked eight spots below them. Alabama's win over Georgia seemingly holds a lot of weight.

Texas already has two losses on its schedule, but the Longhorns also have three of the most impressive wins of anyone in the country against Ohio State, Tennessee and Ole Miss.

UCLA is perhaps one of the most surprising teams in college football this year. Many expected a rebuilding year in Bob Chesney's first season, but the Bruins are undefeated after eight games.

Still, UCLA's most impressive win is over an Oregon team that has since fallen off quite a bit, so the Bruins perhaps still have something to prove.

Notre Dame's ranking of No. 11 perhaps comes as a bit of a surprise, considering the Fighting Irish's only loss came to a top-10 team, but the committee clearly wants to see more from them this year.

Notre Dame will have a big opportunity against Miami this Saturday.

Some of the biggest teams to watch in the coming weeks will be the fringe SEC teams with two losses, like LSU, Tennessee and Missouri. Those squads all have some solid wins by virtue of playing in the SEC, but none can afford to drop another game.

Tuesday's rankings give an idea of how the CFP could shape up, but there are still four weeks left in the regular season, plus conference championships, so anything can happen.

articles.title: College Football Playoffs 2026-27 Bracket Elimination Scenarios in Week 10 After Poll
articles.summary: The first 2026-27 College Football Playoff rankings were unveiled on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
The first 2026-27 College Football Playoff rankings were unveiled on Tuesday night.

Miami sitting in the No. 1 spot doesn't come as a major surprise, as the Hurricanes boast a perfect 8-0 record and also held the top position in the latest Associated Press Top 25 poll .

No. 2 Georgia and No. 3 Utah also sat in the same spot in the CFP rankings compared to the Week 9 AP Top 25 poll, although No. 4 Indiana and No. 5 Alabama both rose in the CFP picture.

With the 12-team playoff format entering its third year, plenty of schools remain hopeful of contending for a CFP berth heading into Week 10.

Still, there are several key matchups that could drastically affect teams looking to avoid being eliminated from the postseason bracket.

No. 9 BYU travels to face Utah on Saturday, representing a clash between the top two teams in the Big 12 standings . The Cougars opened this season with a 6-0 record, but suffered a shocking defeat against UCF on Oct. 24.

While they bounced back with a 27-20 victory over Arizona State on Saturday, a loss to Utah would drop them to 7-2 with a 4-2 mark in the Big 12.

If the Utes can pull out a win and improve to 9-0, they'd gain even more control over the rest of the conference while BYU could begin shifting its focus towards contending for one of the at-large playoff bids.

In the SEC, No. 14 LSU hosts Alabama at Tiger Stadium on Saturday.

The Tigers and Crimson Tide both sit at 6-2, with all four combined losses coming against conference opponents. A third loss with three games left in the regular season would shrink the margin of error for either school, if not end their hopes of clinching a CFP berth entirely.

Another SEC school trying to avoid suffering a third conference defeat of the year is Ole Miss, as the No. 10 Rebels are set to face off against Georgia on Saturday night.

Ole Miss advanced to the CFP semifinals last season, but a loss to the Bulldogs would seriously hurt its hopes of making consecutive playoff appearances. It doesn't help that Rebels standout running back Kewan Lacy's outlook heading into the contest is uncertain due to a shoulder injury .

While Georgia doesn't have as much to lose, head coach Kirby Smart's squad would remain squarely in the conversation for the No. 1 seed in the playoffs with a victory.

articles.title: Man Utd 3-2 Roma: Michael Carrick fights on after Red Devils' comeback win
articles.summary: At 2-0 down Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach looked terminal - but will the win over Roma prove a turning point?
articles.body:
We cannot know how important Bryan Cristante's foot touching the Roma penalty area as Bruno Fernandes took his initial spot-kick at Old Trafford will prove to be for Michael Carrick.

In the moment, as the Roma fans celebrated, and Manchester United trailed 2-0, it seemed catastrophic for the club and terminal for Carrick's position as head coach.

But the video assistant referee (VAR) Carlos del Cerro Grande stepped in, advised a retake was required - and at the very least changed the course of the night.

Fernandes kept his nerve to drive home his second attempt and then, in a frenzied atmosphere, Matheus Cunha scored twice in the final seven minutes. Even without the context of everything that came before the game, it was the most improbable of comebacks.

Even Cunha's sending off soon after, which ensured a nervy ending, would not deny United a first win in 10, bringing some respite after a dreadful few weeks.

How did Carrick feel when the penalty was saved? And what did he say at half-time in response to a desperate first-half display that brought condemnation from legendary United figures Wayne Rooney and Nicky Butt, who were covering the game for Amazon Prime?

In that moment, there was even a sense of deja vu.

"I knew at half-time against Watford," recalled Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in September 2023 of his own dismissal as United boss a couple of years earlier. "At half-time, I told the players it was probably going to be the last time we worked together."

United were two goals down at Vicarage Road at half-time that day. Carrick was on the bench as one of Solskjaer's coaches. They went on to lose 4-1.

We don't need to save anyone's job, says Man Utd captain Fernandes

Man Utd beat Roma - the other great Champions League comebacks

Man Utd produce incredible second-half comeback to beat Roma

Despite the bleakness of the situation, Carrick clearly has a more positive mindset.

"At half-time, I was wanting them to be more positive if anything, and not get too disappointed and frustrated," said Carrick.

"The easiest thing is when you keep trying to do something is feeling sorry for yourself. If something goes wrong, you get disappointed. That's not going to help anybody. We might as well all go home if that's the case. We've got to keep looking for the next moment, the next solution.

"I don't like to keep talking to the lads about what this place can do and the history and what's gone before too much, but it's there.

"This place does magical things, it's done it before and it'll do it over and over again at some point in the future. There's just something in this place that when we do have these types of nights, we do it the hard way.

"But one moment can flip the whole place in a different direction. I spoke about that with the boys. Let's have one moment that can trigger it. And we had that."

Rooney, who was almost pleading with United's players to "show some passion and desire" after a "nothing" first half, could only praise Carrick at the end.

"I think Michael Carrick deserves a lot of credit," said Rooney, "because if you were in his shoes you are thinking how can I change this around?

"Whatever he said to the team at half-time, that got them on the front foot and got that belief in them that they could win the game."

Carrick refused to be downcast - even when Fernandes missed that first penalty.

"I didn't chuckle, I didn't smile, I wasn't happy about it," he said. "But it felt almost like 'there's another moment'.

"But at the same time, I was quite calm because I had a feeling the boys were in a place leaving the changing room that they felt something could happen.

"I have to say, for Bruno to double take that penalty - to have the mentality and finish like that - he deserves a lot of credit."

One great comeback - but what happens now?

While United's victory was certainly well received, it will not mask wider issues.

'Green and gold' protests against the ownership took place before kick-off and during a first-half when the home side were abysmal.

Chants against the Glazer family, minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and director of football Jason Wilcox will not stop just because of this victory, no matter how thrilling.

The sober assessment should also recall United came from behind to beat Atalanta 3-2 at Old Trafford during Solskjaer's time. They lost 5-0 at home to Liverpool four days later. Within a month, the Norwegian had been sacked.

In October 2018, Jose Mourinho was on the brink of dismissal before a Premier League encounter with Newcastle. United trailed 2-0 after 10 minutes but fought back to win. Mourinho lasted 13 more games.

No-one can know how much time Carrick has bought himself with this victory.

"I don't have a crystal ball to know what happens next," he told Amazon Prime. "We move on to the weekend. We've got a really important game here against Aston Villa, which we need to prepare for."

Chief executive Omar Berrada and Wilcox certainly looked much happier at the final whistle than they had done midway through the first half.

Suddenly United look like they can qualify for the next phase of the Champions League. For the first time since September, Carrick's players are enjoying the winning feeling.

But it will mean little unless they can maintain the momentum against Villa, who were getting beaten heavily by Barcelona as Old Trafford was in tumult.

Asked if he will sleep better thanks to the win, Carrick was honest enough to admit that would not be the case.

"Genuinely, no. I don't. Really, I don't," he said. "Whether that's right or wrong, or normal or not, I don't know, but I didn't feel relief. It was more I was genuinely pleased for the players.

"I know how much they care, I know what they're giving. Sometimes it looks like that, sometimes it doesn't, sometimes we play well, sometimes we haven't, and I understand that.

"But I could feel their willingness to do well, and so for them to have to dig really deep, and to see everybody having that feeling that we all crave, that's why we're all here."

'Perfect night' or just 'papering over cracks'?

While the pundits were unanimous in their dismay at United's first-half performance, there was plenty of praise for the second-half revival.

"I said at half-time if you're going to go down, go down fighting. You can accept losing if you've given absolutely everything," said former Denmark goalkeeper Kasper Schmeichel. "They didn't do that in the first half, but they did in the second half.

"Things look a little bit better. Don't get me wrong, the second half is papering over the cracks from the first half, so now it's a case of using this as a benchmark and now having even more of those conversations.

"You have to put your differences aside because you aren't able to change your players now, so you need everyone on side. Everyone has to be on the same page right now."

Being on the same page has seemed like a challenge for Carrick and his players. Lisandro Martinez and Fernandes have both been publicly critical in recent weeks, the targets ranging from the club's hierarchy to the head coach's tactics.

Ex-England defender Stephen Warnock, however, says the narrative set from the win over Roma is "absolutely perfect" for Carrick.

"What's happened is Manchester United have gone in, a vulnerable team, a team lacking in confidence, they've gone 2-0 down - now what's the reaction?

"Now we've just seen the reaction, so we know it's in there. The team are fighting for the manager and they're fighting to turn results around. You've got to fight and show something. When you show fight and start to run for each other, you get more confident in each other and you start to believe that you can do something.

"The Old Trafford fans and that crowd will have turned it up a notch in the second half as soon as that first goal went in and helped the team believe that they could get something out of it.

"It's a perfect night for Michael Carrick."

articles.title: Russell Wilson Interviews for NC State HC Job, Latest Rumors on NFL Icon Amid Philip Rivers Buzz
articles.summary: Former NFL star Russell Wilson interviewed for NC State's head coaching role on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Former NFL star Russell Wilson interviewed for NC State's head coaching role on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Wilson previously played three seasons for the Wolfpack from 2008-10.

He isn't the only former NFL quarterback competing for NC State's vacancy, as CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz previously reported that there's "continued momentum" towards the school hiring Philip Rivers.

Rivers also suited up for the Wolfpack from 2000-03.

He currently coaches at St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama and has informed NC State that he wants to finish the current high school season before potentially moving to the college level, per ESPN .

The Wolfpack started their search for a new face to patrol the sidelines after Dave Doeren was fired as head coach following a 3-4 start to the 2026 season. Todd Goebbel serves as the school's interim coach.

As for Wilson, he spent his first three years with the Wolfpack in college before joining Wisconsin. He threw for 8,545 yards during his tenure at NC State, while his 76 passing touchdowns rank No. 2 on the team's all-time leaderboard .

Wilson was eventually selected by the Seattle Seahawks with a third-round pick in the 2012 NFL draft, earning 10 Pro Bowl nods and capturing a Super Bowl title throughout his playing career.

The 37-year-old appeared in six games for the New York Giants during his 2025 campaign before announcing his retirement after the season came to a close.

Now, Wilson operates as an NFL analyst for CBS Sports.

articles.title: Everything CFP Committee Chair Said About Notre Dame, Ohio State, Alabama, More After 1st Rankings
articles.summary: The first College Football Playoff rankings were revealed on Tuesday, and naturally, there were a few decisions to be explained by the committee.
articles.body:
The first College Football Playoff rankings were revealed on Tuesday, and naturally, there were a few decisions to be explained by the committee.

One of the biggest ones had to do with Notre Dame, which was ranked No. 11 despite having just one loss. Hunter Yurachek, a member of the committee, said it was due to a lack of a big win.

"They don't have that signature win right now. They lost in their only Top 25 matchup so far," Yurachek said on the ESPN rankings show.

Alabama was ranked eight spots ahead of Tennessee, despite being blown out by the Vols just over two weeks ago. That decision came down to the Crimson Tide's resume.

"To compare teams head to head, they have to be in the same pod," Yurachek said .

Similar to Alabama and Tennessee, Indiana was ranked eight spots higher than Ohio State despite losing to the Buckeyes. Yurachek explained that Ohio State's double-digit loss to USC last week led to the drastic discrepancy.

"I think the committee still has a lot of respect for Ohio State and who they are as a football team this year, and they do have a very impressive win on the road at Indiana that came down to a wire to a catch in the end zone that would just miss by inches, but they didn't look like the same Ohio State team this past weekend against Southern Cal," Yurachek said .

Yurachek also said that the committee isn't penalizing Ohio State for quarterback Julian Sayin's injury.

"Ohio State is not being penalized for having a quarterback that's out there, they're being evaluated as a team with another quarterback in the lineup for them," he said .

There is no stopping fans from overreacting to the first College Football Playoff ranking, but it's worth noting how different these rankings could look next week.

Notre Dame will face Miami on Saturday, and a win over the Hurricanes at home would surely put the Fighting Irish right among the top teams in college football in next week's ranking.

Alabama has a tough matchup against LSU this week, and a third loss for the Crimson Tide would give the committee no choice but to demote them out of the top-12.

If Tennessee handles business against No. 6 Kentucky, the Vols could very well jump their rival Alabama in the next rankings.

There are plenty of other matchups with CFP implications, like BYU's matchup with Utah, Texas' game against Missouri and Ole Miss' battle with Georgia.

It's safe to say the rankings will shift some over the next week, and could look completely different at the end of the season.

articles.title: College Football Playoff rankings: Miami leads first rankings of 2026; Notre Dame, Ohio State outside top 10
articles.summary: Fans who are confused or annoyed with the inaugural CFP rankings can take solace. Week 10 should provide a lot more clarity.
articles.body:
Miami is ranked atop the season's first set of College Football Playoff rankings .

The undefeated Hurricanes are No. 1 in the AP Top 25 and were the unsurprising top team in Tuesday night's inaugural rankings of 2026. But you didn't have to go very far down the rankings to find some stark differences between the AP poll and the CFP selection committee's rankings.

Notre Dame, which is at No. 4 in the AP poll, was ranked No. 11 on Tuesday night. The one-loss Irish missed out on the College Football Playoff a season ago after the committee moved them behind Miami in the final set of rankings even though neither team played on conference championship weekend.

Miami, of course, beat Notre Dame in Week 1. And the two teams play again on Saturday night in a game that somehow looks even more pivotal for the playoff than it did 24 hours ago.

If Notre Dame loses to Miami again, will it miss the College Football Playoff again?

The Irish have games against Boston College, SMU and Syracuse remaining. All of those teams are unranked. The Irish have a very clear path to 10-2 if they lose to the Hurricanes. And given the way the committee appears to be valuing strength of schedule, Notre Dame could find itself on the outside looking in for a second straight season.

CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek — the athletic director at Arkansas — cited Notre Dame's schedule as the main reason why the Irish were at No. 11.

"When you look at Notre Dame's schedule and the wins they have versus the teams that are ahead of them, they don't have that signature win right now," Yurachek said on ESPN. "They lost in their only top-25 matchup at BYU, their next-best win is at a neutral site. They've got a great opportunity in front of them at home versus Miami to get that signature win that I think they need to move up in the rankings."

The Irish are ranked behind three two-loss teams. Georgia, Utah and Indiana filled out the top four with two-loss Alabama a surprising No. 5. The Crimson Tide are eight spots ahead of Tennessee. The Volunteers have an identical 6-2 record and beat the Crimson Tide by 16 points.

Alabama is also ahead of Kentucky. The Tide handed the Wildcats their only loss of the season in Week 2. Texas is at No. 7 ahead of undefeated UCLA. BYU and Ole Miss are the last two teams in the top 10.

How much does strength of schedule matter?

Ohio State's losses are to No. 7 Texas and No. 20 USC. The Buckeyes, who handed Indiana its only loss of the season, are at No. 12 behind the Fighting Irish as they're likely to be without QB Julian Sayin for the rest of the season . That injury is clearly a driving factor why Ohio State is outside the top 10.

Overall, 10 teams with one loss or fewer are in the first set of rankings. Four of those teams are outside of the top 10. Texas Tech is at No. 15, Wake Forest is at No. 16 and Boise State is at No. 25.

Of the six two-loss teams inside the top 15, six are from the SEC. It's clear the committee values the SEC as the top conference in the country and that view comes after the SEC spent the spring and summer pushing for strength of schedule to be a greater factor considered by the committee.

Right now, it looks very plausible that a three-loss SEC team could make the playoff as Alabama did a season ago. This season, Yurachek credited Alabama's win over Kentucky and wins over Mississippi State (when QB Kamario Taylor was available) and South Carolina as to why the Crimson Tide were in the top five.

If you're confused, annoyed, frustrated or any combination of the above with the first set of rankings, we have some good news for you: Week 10 is going to give us a lot of clarity.

Not only does No. 1 Miami play No. 11 Notre Dame, but No. 2 Georgia visits No. 10 Ole Miss, No. 9 BYU goes to No. 3 Utah, No. 5 Alabama heads to No. 14 LSU, No. 13 Tennessee hosts No. 6 Kentucky and No. 7 Texas visits No. 18 Missouri. There's a very real chance that all three two-loss teams in the top 10 could have three losses by the end of Saturday.

Or, if you're a fan of chaos, we could have an even bigger morass of two-loss teams. That's possible too. But we're betting on things sorting themselves out at least somewhat before the second set of rankings.
